questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the file state that the measures could not wait for the insurer's instruction because of imminent danger (Gefahr im Verzug)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the policy, or the file, show that the policy does not include the separate supplementary insurance for simple theft away from home (einfacher Diebstahl auswärts)?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the file state that the original purchase vouchers for all of the stolen or damaged items cannot be obtained, or only at considerable cost (not even as a duplicate from the seller)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Is a bicycle among the stolen or damaged items?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the file state that measures to reduce the loss are still to be taken (not yet carried out)?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Does the file state that household contents were stolen or damaged by a theft outside the insured location that was neither a burglary (the thief forcibly entered the building or a room of it, or broke open a container in it, or unlocked it with the correct keys or codes that the thief had obtained by burglary or robbery; a vehicle is not a container) or a robbery (theft under threat or use of violence against the policyholder or a member of the household, or while they could not resist because of unconsciousness, accident or death; pickpocketing and trick theft are not robbery)?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Does the file state that traces of the theft (for example pry marks, a broken lock, window or container) have been removed or altered, or are to be removed or altered, by the policyholder or on their behalf, for example by repair or cleaning?

text:
Dear Ms Schmid,

I'm writing about a theft on 27 August 2026, and I have to say at the start that I don't know where exactly it happened. That morning I rode to Schaffhausen station and left my bike there with my work bag clipped to the rack. In the evening I took the bus home because of the rain. Emma Ammann, who I share the flat with, says she walked past the station, saw the bike, and rode it home and put it in our shed at Brunnenrain 37. She's fairly sure about that. I'm not, because I never saw it in the shed, and by the next morning it was gone either way. So it may have been taken at the station or from our shed, and neither of us can prove which.

The good news is that the bike has a small GPS tracker under the saddle, and since yesterday the app shows it in a yard in Neuhausen. I haven't been there yet. Tomorrow morning I'm going with a police officer to get it back.

I should be honest that I never took the extra CSS cover for simple theft away from home, I decided against it when I signed up in 2023.

I'm going to Neuhausen tomorrow without waiting for your answer, and I hope you understand why. The tracker has moved twice in two days, and if I wait even a few more days the bike could be sold or taken apart and it would be gone for good.

It's a normal men's bicycle, a dark green touring bike, no motor or battery. With the bag, my laptop that was in it and the lights, the loss comes to CHF 8,850.

I have no receipts at all. The bike was bought second-hand from a neighbour, the laptop was a present, and the bag came from a flea market. There's no shop I could ask for a duplicate.

Kind regards,
Nina Tanner
